key_insight: A single contrastive geometric model (ConGLUDe) unifies structure- and ligand-based drug design by aligning geometric protein representations with ligand information, enabling joint training and cross-modal transfer between protein structure and ligand data.
problem_solved: Existing workflows treat structure-based and ligand-based methods separately because of different data types and modeling assumptions, preventing scalable joint learning and reuse of knowledge across tasks.
method: Contrastive geometric learning to align protein-level geometric encodings with ligand or predicted-binding embeddings in a shared representation space.
A geometric protein encoder that produces whole-protein representations plus implicit embeddings of predicted binding regions, enabling cross-modal supervision without separate pocket annotation.
Unified training procedure that leverages both structural data (protein coordinates) and ligand data (SMILES/graphs) so a single model supports structure- and ligand-centered downstream tasks.
impact: ConGLUDe enables AI/ML practitioners to train one model that transfers between structure- and ligand-based tasks, improving data efficiency and simplifying pipelines for virtual screening, lead optimization, and generative design.
visual_elements: Schematic of ConGLUDe architecture showing geometric protein encoder, ligand encoder, and contrastive alignment objective between embeddings.
Before/after diagram: separate ligand- and structure-based pipelines vs. unified ConGLUDe pipeline.
Embedding visualization (e.g., t-SNE/UMAP) showing proteins and ligands co-located in a shared latent space after contrastive training.
Use-case icons: virtual screening, ligand generation, binding-site prediction with arrows showing model reuse across tasks.
paper_title: Contrastive Geometric Learning Unlocks Unified Structure- and Ligand-Based Drug Design
paper_authors: Lisa Schneckenreiter, Sohvi Luukkonen, Lukas Friedrich, Daniel Kuhn, Günter Klambauer
